items.fdcDescription: Pork bacon, smoked or cured, cooked
items.notes: Manual semantic review binds Cook4Me 'Chopped pancetta (or diced bacon)' to USDA FNDDS 'Pork bacon, smoked or cured, cooked'. Bacon is explicitly one of the permitted source alternatives, and the target's own pinned evidence contains this exact cooked cured-bacon record. Confidence remains medium because pancetta can differ from smoked bacon in curing, smoking, fat distribution, and cooking state; this review does not infer which alternative is used in every recipe instance.

Manual semantic review binds Cook4Me 'Dried okra' to USDA SR Legacy 'Okra, raw'. The target is explicitly okra and its own pinned evidence contains this exact okra record. Drying preserves the underlying vegetable identity but substantially changes water content and nutrient concentration, so confidence remains medium and the record is used as a same-food proxy only; this review does not generalize to fried, pickled, or sauced okra.

Manual semantic review binds Cook4Me 'Fresh, chopped tarragon' to USDA SR Legacy 'Spices, tarragon, dried'. The target is explicitly tarragon and its own pinned evidence contains this exact tarragon record. Chopping does not change identity, but drying strongly changes water content and nutrient concentration, so confidence remains medium and the record is used as a same-herb proxy only; this review does not imply that the Cook4Me ingredient is dried.

Manual semantic review binds Cook4Me 'Organic peas in pods' to USDA SR Legacy 'Peas, edible-podded, raw'. The target explicitly specifies peas in pods and its own pinned evidence contains this edible-podded raw-pea record. Organic production does not change the food identity. Confidence remains medium because the source wording does not prove whether the entire pod is intended to be eaten or only the peas are shelled before use; this review does not generalize to canned peas or dried legumes.

Manual semantic review binds Cook4Me 'Savory biscuits' to USDA SR Legacy 'Crackers, water biscuits'. The target explicitly identifies a savory biscuit, and its own pinned evidence ranks water biscuits first. This is a better form match than sweet cookies, baby biscuits, dry mix, or unbaked dough. Confidence remains medium because the exact flour, fat, salt, brand, and cracker style are unspecified; this review does not generalize to sweet biscuits or cookies.

Manual semantic review binds Cook4Me 'Wheat groats' to USDA SR Legacy 'Wheat, durum'. The target is explicitly a whole-grain wheat preparation and its own pinned evidence contains this durum-wheat record. Confidence remains medium because the catalog does not identify wheat variety, degree of cracking, parboiling, or cooked-versus-dry weight state; this review preserves the wheat-grain identity and does not generalize to buckwheat groats, wheat bran, germ, flour, or bread.
